newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds weather issuance, some junk hit.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds weather issuance, some junk hit.

text.p: Some big U.S. corporate issues were deftly handled by investors on Tuesday and most spreads held firm to U.S. Treasuries, dealers said.

High-yield new issues were also put away with little resistance, traders said. Bargain-hunting sent some secondary junk prices higher, but troubled MobileMedia and CAI Wireless Systems Inc eroded further, traders added.

Back in investment grades, issuance of nearly $2 billion in debt dwarfed secondary trade and prices ended marginally lower in sympathy with Treasuries. The U.S. Treasury long bond closed down 11/32 to yield 6.49 percent.

Issuance was topped by $1.1 billion 6.70 percent 10-year Aa1/AA-plus rated subordinated notes from Deutsche Bank Financial Inc, a unit of Deutsche Bank AG via Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. The notes were priced at a spread of 54 basis points over the Treasury curve.
The size of the offering was increased from $1.0 billion to meet investor demand, the lead manager said.
Elsewhere, Philip Morris Cos issued $500 million A2/A rated seven-year notes as 6.80s to yield 73 basis points over the curve via a Goldman, Sachs & Co syndicate.
Nike Inc issued $200 million in 6.375 percent seven-year notes to yield 34 basis points over Treasuries via joint managers Goldman Sachs & Co and Salomon Brothers.
The Nike deal was upped in size from $150 million.
Further down the rating spectrum, the National Power Corp (NAPOCOR) of the Philippines issued $360 milllion of Ba2/BB rated government guaranteed debt in a two-part offering via Salomon Brothers.
The first tranche, $200 million in 10-year 7.875 percent guaranteeed bonds, was priced to yield 167 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
The second tranche, $160 million in 8.40 percent 20-year bonds, was priced to yield 190 basis points over Treasuries.

Turning to the high-yield secondary, Trump Castle Funding notes benefitted from bargain hunting and gained about two points by session's end, traders said. The notes, which had sent lower after news the Rank Organisation Plc would not followthrough on an expected $50 million investment, were quoted at 86-1/2 bid at the close.

On the flip side, MobileMedia's 9-3/8 percent debt of 2007 faded five points to 43 bid, 44 offer after the company said it may seek Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. MobileMedia announced last week that it did not make November interest payments on the notes by the end of a 30-day grace period.
CAI Wireless Systems Inc debt dipped again and was bid 46 bid, 50 offer, one trader said.

High-yield issuance featured $175 million units of 10-year senior discount notes from Colt Telecom Group via lead manager Morgan Stanley & Co Inc. The zeros were priced at 55.875 with warrants for two percent of the company.
The issue was quoted at 57-1/2 bid before the close.
